title: Console backend endpoints for audit export destination management + test delivery
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
Build the Console-facing backend endpoints required to manage SIEM-ready Audit Export destinations (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3) and to run a safe “test delivery” / “verify credentials” action from Console.

This ticket is specifically the Console backend/API gateway layer that Console UI will call. Control-plane data model + internal APIs are owned by ENG-13921 / PR redwood#28411; RBAC/audit logging gating is ENG-13933 / PR redwood#28427.

Problem
- Console UI needs a stable API surface to CRUD export destinations, validate filters/credentials, show destination health, and initiate a test event send.
- We need consistent error semantics for UI (actionable error messages + copyable error_id) without leaking secrets.
- Must be gated behind per-tenant beta flag and RBAC.

Scope
1) Destination management endpoints (Console backend)
- List destinations for workspace/tenant
- Create destination
- Update destination
- Delete destination
- Get destination detail (including health/status fields)

2) Test delivery / verify credentials endpoint
- "Send test event" from Console that triggers connector-specific validation and emits a synthetic audit event (or sink-specific write) with a clearly marked test marker.
- Should return a structured result the UI can render (success, warnings, failure category, error_id, troubleshooting hints).

Non-goals
- Implementing sink connectors (owned by ENG-13924/25/26)
- Implementing the worker queue/replay tooling (ENG-13923/13934)
- Full Console UI (ENG-13930)

Proposed API (Console backend, external)
- GET /v1/console/audit-export/destinations
- POST /v1/console/audit-export/destinations
- GET /v1/console/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}
- PATCH /v1/console/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}
- DELETE /v1/console/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}
- POST /v1/console/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}:test

Notes:
- We should align naming with the existing Console route patterns, but keep parity with the audit-export control-plane service so that Console UI doesn’t need per-destination type branching beyond form fields.
- The :test endpoint should be idempotent-ish from a UI perspective (safe to click twice); however, the sink may receive multiple test records. Ensure the event includes test=true so customers can filter.

AuthZ / gating
- Feature flag: tenant/workspace allowlist for SIEM export beta (PR redwood#28445). All endpoints should return 404 (not 403) when the feature is not enabled, to reduce feature discovery.
- RBAC permission required: "security.audit_export.manage" (final permission name per ENG-13933). Enforce on all write endpoints and on :test.
- Read endpoints should require at least "security.audit_export.read" (if we split read vs manage); otherwise reuse manage for beta simplicity.

Secret handling
- Destination create/update accepts credentials payload, but response must never echo secrets.
- For Splunk: accept token; for Datadog: accept API key; for S3: accept role ARN / external ID or access key material depending on final auth model (per design spec/ADR). Store via control-plane secrets integration.
- Log redaction: ensure request logging middleware is configured to redact known credential fields.

Test delivery semantics
- Splunk HEC: send a single small event with a dedicated sourcetype (if configured) or a fixed event marker; classify 401/403 vs 4xx vs 5xx vs timeout as separate error categories.
- Datadog: send a single log event with tags {source:redwood, service:audit-export, env:<env>, redwood_test:true}; handle 429 throttling with a short backoff and a bounded retry (do not hang UI).
- S3: write a small object into a "test/" prefix (or configured prefix + "/_redwood_test/") with server-side encryption settings applied; if we can’t safely write, perform a HeadBucket / GetBucketLocation + KMS encrypt permission check. Return clear guidance about required IAM actions.

Response and error model
- Standard envelope should include:
  - request_id (from gateway)
  - error_id (stable identifier for support)
  - category: auth | permissions | throttling | validation | network | server | unknown
  - retryable: true/false
  - user_message (safe for UI)
  - debug_message (only in internal logs)

Observability
- Emit metrics for:
  - console_audit_export_api_requests_total{route,method,status}
  - console_audit_export_test_requests_total{destination_type,result,category}
  - console_audit_export_test_latency_ms{destination_type}
- Log a single structured event for :test start/end with destination_id, destination_type, workspace_id, result, error_id.
- Ensure no secret fields are included in logs.

References
- Confluence PRD: siem-ready-audit-export-beta-prd
- Confluence design spec: audit-export-filtering-and-delivery-guarantees
- Control plane APIs: redwood PR #28411
- RBAC + audit logging for config changes: redwood PR #28427
- Beta feature flag gating: redwood PR #28445
- Console UI ticket: ENG-13930
acceptance_criteria: Console backend exposes CRUD endpoints for audit export destinations (list/create/get/update/delete) and they successfully proxy/translate to the audit-export control-plane APIs.
POST :test triggers sink-specific verification and returns a structured result (success/failure category, retryable, error_id) suitable for Console rendering.
All endpoints are gated by beta feature flag (disabled tenants see 404) and enforce RBAC permissions on write actions.
No credential values are returned in any API response; request/response logging is redacted for credential fields.
OpenAPI/route docs updated and validated by Console team; minimal integration test coverage added for success + common failures (401/403, 429, timeout).
Metrics + structured logs shipped for :test and CRUD endpoints, with dashboards hooks added per observability plan.
implementation_notes:
Implementation approach:
- Add a Console API module (redwood/console-api) that calls the audit-export control-plane service (internal) using service auth.
- Define typed DTOs for destination types to avoid leaking internal schemas directly into Console contracts.
- For :test, prefer calling an internal audit-export service endpoint that performs the actual connector call, rather than having Console backend directly call Splunk/Datadog/S3. If we must call sinks directly for beta, keep sink-specific code behind a minimal interface and reuse existing connector libs from audit-log-exporter.
- Ensure that :test is rate-limited per destination/workspace to prevent abuse (e.g., 5/min) and use a short timeout (<=10s) with a clear "test queued" fallback if the worker path is asynchronous.
- Validate destination ownership (workspace_id) server-side; never accept workspace_id from the client for update/delete beyond path scoping.

Open questions:
- Do we want :test to write a real audit event into the export pipeline (end-to-end), or a connector-only direct send? End-to-end is better fidelity but can be slower and harder to interpret.
- Should create/update do strict credential verification synchronously, or only on :test + background health checks?
- Final permission names and whether we split read vs manage during beta (confirm with Security Eng).
